assessment.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Rudého moře a Adenského zálivu zůstává napjatá, což dokazuje nejnovější incident, při kterém ozbrojená skupina napadla a převzala kontrolu nad nákladní lodí u pobřeží Jemenu. Současně pokračují regionální střety a útoky na strategickou infrastrukturu včetně dronových aktivit a raketových útoků, které nadále ohrožují klíčové námořní trasy.
assessment.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden remains highly tense, highlighted by a recent incident where an armed group boarded and seized control of a cargo ship off the coast of Yemen. Simultaneously, regional clashes and attacks on strategic infrastructure, including drone activity and missile strikes, continue to threaten key maritime routes.

recommendations.reason_cs: Přetrvávající útoky v Rudém moři a vysoké ceny paliv nutí lodní společnosti držet vysoké sazby za přepravu a těžit z delších tras kolem Afriky.
recommendations.reason_en: Persistent attacks in the Red Sea and high fuel costs force shipping companies to maintain elevated freight rates and benefit from longer routes around Africa.

recommendations.sector_en: Defense Industry (e.g. RTX, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems)

recommendations.reason_en: Escalating tensions in the Middle East and high demand for air defense and military equipment guarantee a strong influx of government contracts.

recommendations.sector_cs: Ropa a Plyn (např. Shell, BP, Chevron)
recommendations.reason_cs: Ropa Brent se drží v blízkosti 96 USD za barel, protože hrozby v Hormuzském průlivu a útoky Houthiů udržují fyzické dodávky napjaté navzdory slabším výhledům poptávky.
recommendations.reason_en: Brent crude is holding near $96 per barrel as threats in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks keep physical supplies tight despite weaker demand forecasts.

recommendations.sector_cs: Evropský Spotřební sektor & Autoprůmysl (např. Volvo, BMW)
recommendations.reason_cs: Zpoždění dodávek v důsledku krizí v námořní dopravě a rostoucí náklady na energie a paliva nadále negativně doléhají na marže těchto společností.
recommendations.reason_en: Supply delays driven by maritime transport crises and rising energy and fuel costs continue to weigh negatively on the profit margins of these companies.

recommendations.sector_cs: Pražská burza: ČEZ, Komerční banka, Erste Group
recommendations.sector_en: Prague Stock Exchange: ČEZ, Komerční banka, Erste Group
recommendations.reason_cs: Domácí tituly jsou vůči geopolitickým šokům na Blízkém východě relativně izolované, jejich valuace jsou však stabilní a odrážejí spíše lokální makroekonomický vývoj.
recommendations.reason_en: Domestic equities are relatively insulated from Middle Eastern geopolitical shocks, but their valuations remain stable, reflecting local macroeconomic trends instead.

recommendations.sector_cs: Evropské blue-chips (např. Airbus, TotalEnergies, Allianz, Rheinmetall)
recommendations.sector_en: European blue-chips (e.g. Airbus, TotalEnergies, Allianz, Rheinmetall)
recommendations.reason_cs: Smíšený vliv energetické krize a geopolitického napětí vytváří protichůdné tlaky; zatímco energetika a obrana profitují, širší cyklické firmy čelí protivětru.
recommendations.reason_en: The mixed impact of the energy crisis and geopolitical tension creates conflicting pressures; while energy and defense benefit, broader cyclical firms face headwinds.

assessment.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech se očekává setrvání cen ropy poblíž 96-100 USD za barel pod vlivem přetrvávajících útoků v Rudém moři a napětí v Hormuzském průlivu.
assessment.forecast_en: Over the coming days, oil prices are expected to remain near $96-$100 per barrel driven by ongoing attacks in the Red Sea and tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.
assessment.forecast_review_cs: Předchozí předpověď se plně potvrdila, neboť ceny ropy se drží v očekávaném rozmezí 96-100 USD za barel a útoky v oblasti pokračují.
assessment.forecast_review_en: The previous forecast was fully confirmed as oil prices remain within the expected $96-$100 range and regional attacks persist.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Saturday it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the Iran-aligned group towards the Saudi town of Al Shuqaiq, adding that the debris came down without causing any civilian casualties.

Al Shuqaiq, on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast in Jazan province, is home to major desalination and power generation facilities supplying water and electricity to the kingdom's southern regions.

Armed group boards cargo ship off Yemen and takes control, UKMTO says

Armed individuals boarded a cargo ship 64 nautical miles southwest of Yemen's Balhaf at 0630 GMT and took control of the vessel, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Saturday, citing the ship's master.

UKMTO said authorities had been informed and advised vessels in the area to proceed with caution.

A European Union naval mission also reported a piracy incident in the area on Saturday, but it was not immediately clear if it was the same ship whose attack was reported by UKMTO.

Reporting by Reuters

“This unbreakable bond [with Iran] requires Baghdad to remain vigilant on the issue of borders so that it does not become a tool of the enemies of Islam or give in to the policies of the criminal Trump,” Mokhber said.

Personnel at RAF Lakenheath were told to take cover on 13 November after “suspected unauthorised drone activity”. The US air force confirmed the so-called Charlie alert at the time, the second-highest threat level, but released few details. Sirens could be heard at the base. Iran is suspected of being involved.

articles.title: Pezeshkian announces return of damaged South Pars gas pipelines to production
articles.summary:
Pezeshkian announces return of damaged South Pars gas pipelines to production

Iran has repaired three gas pipelines damaged in the early weeks of the US-Israeli war, returning them to production at the South Pars gas field, the country’s state-run Mehr news agency said.

The agency said that lines 1 and 4 of the fourth refinery and line 3 of the sixth refinery were back in operation, adding 20 million cubic metres of gas a day to Iran's gas output capacity.

President Masoud Pezeshkian announced the development, saying: “Getting through the winter without cutting off electricity, gas, and fuel needed for production requires the support of the people, the efforts of producers, and improving infrastructure.”

War damage to Iran’s energy infrastructure has compounded energy shortages. As winter draws close, authorities have announced two-hour electricity cuts in parts of the country.
